data.text:
F20 is fixed at records 95 and 96 and verified independently of the implementer that
wrote it. The verification that matters is not that the three named columns are now on
the list, because a check that only knew those three would pass again the moment a
fourth arrived. It is that the check can no longer be answered by reading a column name.

Measured: `alter table public.evidence add column recipient_postcode text`, with no
comment and a name nowhere near `buyer%`, and the suite then fails with "1 of the 121
columns in schema public that can hold a sentence say neither that they hold buyer data
nor why a buyer's name and address cannot reach them: evidence.recipient_postcode
(text)". The old check would have passed it in silence, because its query could only
return columns already named for the buyer. The column was dropped again and the suite
is back to 86 passing.

The classification is not a rubber stamp. 120 columns carry a comment where 6 did
before, and they have 94 distinct openings between them, so they were written rather
than pasted. Three worth quoting, because each records something the next ticket needs:
`audit_events.payload` is classified not buyer PII as a constraint on SEEN-032 and
SEEN-034 rather than as a fact, since a draft reply copied into it would put buyer data
in an append-only table no expiry can reach; `settlement_lines.description` names the
claim it rests on as unverified against live data and says it is the comment to change
when SEEN-015 or SEEN-026 settles it; and `connections.scopes` explains why an array of
text is a candidate at all, which is that a list of strings holds an address as readily
as one string does.

One count in the brief this round was given was wrong, and the implementer corrected it
rather than adopting it. The measurement handed over said 119 candidates; there are 120.
The query behind the 119 matched `text`, `character varying` and `jsonb` and did not
match array types, so `connections.scopes`, a `text[]`, was missing from it. The fix
enumerates by catalogue type including arrays, which is why the RED says 120.

Two limits of the fix, stated rather than left to be discovered:

- The classification governs stored columns only. A view's columns are derived, so a
  view could re-expose a classified column under another name; part 6 governs whether a
  view is reachable at all and nothing classifies what a view selects.
- `evidence.storage_path` is classified not buyer PII and the file it points at is not.
  A proof of delivery names the buyer inside the object, so clearing
  `evidence.buyer_name` and `evidence.buyer_address` does not expire the storage object.
  Nothing in this schema can reach storage. SEEN-083 has to.

And three things found and not fixed: `messages` and `message_threads` have no
participant or from-address column, so a buyer's email address has nowhere to go today
and whatever SEEN-061 and SEEN-062 add for it will fail part 7 until they classify it,
which is the intended behaviour; `claim_events.detail` is the milder twin of
`audit_events.payload`; and the claim_text tension itself is recorded, not resolved.

F21, F22 and F23 of record 88 remain open. F19's part 6 is untouched apart from its
header count.
